lesson: Continue an AB pattern, and spot a mistake in it.

pages.art: A narrow, crooked alley in the old part of a city on a summer morning: honey-coloured stone walls, a stone arch, small windows with wooden shutters, a strip of blue sky above. At the far end, a green wooden door with a stone step. A young tiler pushes a small cart stacked with square tiles, plain yellow and plain green (no patterns or letters on them), into the alley. Feeling: sunny, quiet, the start of something. Calm area: the strip of sky across the top.

Ilan (4) sits on the step of his green door, chin in his hands, watching. A few steps away the tiler kneels and presses a yellow tile down beside a green one; the path is a single line of big square tiles, one tile wide, running along the alley floor. A small curved line shows the click of the tile (no letters). Feeling: calm, absorbed. Calm area: the stone wall across the top.

Ilan nods along, mouth open in song, one hand beating time on his knee; the tiler glances up at him and smiles while setting the next tile. The line of tiles alternates yellow, green, yellow, green. Feeling: rhythm, friendship without words. Calm area: the stone wall across the top.

Seen from above, like a map of the alley: the yellow-green line of tiles stretches from the corner most of the way to the green door. Shadows show morning light. Ilan stands on his step, the tiler kneels at the end of the line. Feeling: progress, getting closer. Calm area: the plain alley floor along the bottom.

A neighbour, a woman with a shopping basket on her arm, has stopped beside the tiler; they talk and laugh. The tiler looks up at her, not at his hands, while setting another tile. Ilan watches from his step. Feeling: friendly chatter, a small slip about to happen. Calm area: the stone wall across the top.

Close on the line of tiles, seen from Ilan's height: yellow, green, yellow, green, green. The two green tiles side by side stand out clearly. At the edge of the picture, Ilan's frowning face and pointing eyes. Feeling: something is not right; a puzzle for the reader. Calm area: the alley floor along the bottom.

Ilan stands on one foot on his step, lips pressed together, wobbling, bursting to speak, while the two grown-ups go on chatting. Feeling: polite waiting, funny effort. Calm area: the stone wall across the top.

The neighbour walks away round the corner, waving goodbye over her shoulder. Ilan has jumped off his step and points straight at the second green tile, his whole arm stretched out. Feeling: finally, his turn to speak. Calm area: the stone wall across the top.

The tiler, kneeling, laughs with his head back and one hand on his forehead; with the other hand he lifts the extra green tile out. A yellow tile waits beside it. Ilan beams. Feeling: a mistake owned with a laugh; respect between the two. Calm area: the stone wall across the top.

The tiler, kneeling, holds out the last two tiles, one yellow and one green, on his flat palms; Ilan carefully lays the yellow one in the gap at the end of the line, the green one waiting in his other hand. The tiler steadies the tile beside Ilan's fingers. Feeling: trust, concentration, pride. Calm area: the alley floor along the bottom.

Seen from above again: the finished path, yellow, green, yellow, green, from the corner of the alley right up to the green door's step. Ilan and the tiler stand side by side at the end, admiring it. Feeling: complete, orderly, pleased. Calm area: the plain alley floor along the bottom.

Last picture of the book, the next morning: Ilan hops along the dry path, one foot in the air, mid-hop on a yellow tile, arms out for balance. The tiler, at the corner with his empty cart, claps. Soft morning light on the stone. Feeling: joy, rhythm, home. Calm area: the strip of sky across the top.

shots.action: 16 s. Scene 1, the alley. A summer morning in the old part of a city: stone walls, an arch, shutters, a strip of sky, the green door at the end. The tiler wheels his cart of tiles in. Keep the lower fifth calm for captions in every shot. Music rule for the whole film: every tile that goes down sounds one note on the beat, a low note for yellow and a high note for green.
8 s. The tiler kneels, smooths a flat bed for the tiles and sets the first one down on the beat.
6 s. Close on the cart: plain yellow and plain green square tiles stacked side by side.
12 s. Ilan on his doorstep, chin in his hands. Tiles go down on the beat: yellow low, green high, yellow low, green high.
sound: tile notes on the beat: low, high, low, high

shots.action: 9 s. Ilan nods and sings along with the notes.
7 s. The tiler notices, smiles, and lays the next tiles exactly on Ilan's beat.
14 s. Days pass in three short beats: the shadows swing across the alley, Ilan's shirt changes colour, the path grows closer to the door.
sound: the tune repeating, a little fuller each day

shots.action: 8 s. Scene 2, the slip. A neighbour with a shopping basket stops by the tiler.
6 s. The tiler answers, laughing, looking at her while his hands keep working.
10 s. Close on the tiles going down: low, high, low, high, and then a high note again, off the beat. The music hiccups.
sound: low, high, low, high, high: the last note late and wrong

shots.action: 7 s. Ilan frowns.
7 s. Ilan counts along the path with one finger.
sound: the tile notes, played softly one by one under his voice

shots.action: 4 s. Hold on the two green tiles side by side: the viewer's moment to spot it.
8 s. Ilan opens his mouth, then closes it: the grown-ups are still chatting.
12 s. Ilan waits on one foot, then the other, wobbling. A small comic dance of patience; no words.
6 s. The neighbour waves goodbye and goes round the corner.
6 s. Ilan jumps off his step and points.
8 s. The tiler looks, looks again, and laughs.
10 s. He lifts the green tile out and sets a yellow one in: its low note lands right on the beat, and the tune is whole again.
sound: the low note, on the beat

shots.action: 8 s. Scene 3, Ilan's turn. The tiler holds out the last two tiles.
8 s. Ilan looks at the last tile in the line, thinking.
11 s. Ilan lays yellow, then green, very carefully, the tiler's hand beside his: two notes, both on the beat.
14 s. Wide from above: the finished path. The camera glides along it from the corner to the green door, one note per tile: the whole tune at last.
8 s. The next morning: the path is dry; Ilan stands at the corner, ready.
12 s. Ilan hops the path, one hop per tile, each hop playing its note.
sound: the tile tune, one note per hop

shots.action: 6 s. The tiler, at the corner with his empty cart, claps.
6 s. Ilan sits on his doorstep and looks back along his path, smiling.
16 s. Closing image: the alley from above, the yellow-green path like a line of music leading to the green door. Hold the still picture 6 s while the music ends, then stop. No autoplay.

steps.picture: A grown-up and a child, both in sun hats, gather fallen leaves from the ground and fist-sized stones into a basket under a shady tree.
On the ground, a line: leaf, stone, leaf, stone, and an empty space at the end. The child holds a leaf over the space, ready to put it down; the grown-up watches.
The child lays a new line (leaf, leaf, stone, leaf, leaf, stone) and points to the end; the grown-up crouches to add the next piece.
